title: Fans and the next audience
hook: A toy launch succeeds with early fans. What happens as the audience mix changes?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Keep within-segment rates separate from audience composition when transferring launch evidence.

misconception: A strong overall early-launch rate predicts the same rate in the mainstream audience.
objective: Keep within-segment rates separate from audience composition when transferring launch evidence.

claims.text: The named work is Crossing the Chasm, by Geoffrey A. Moore, candidate publication year 1991.
claims.source: Geoffrey A. Moore, Crossing the Chasm (1991); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Crossing the Chasm distinguishes early adopters from mainstream customers who require different reasons to adopt.
claims.source: Geoffrey A. Moore, Crossing the Chasm (1991); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated selection model: A inputs [90, 90, 10, 10] yield 82; B inputs [10, 90, 90, 10] yield 18. Prediction correct option 18. A averages {A}%; B averages {B}%. Segment rates stay 90% and 10%; only the weights change as the audience shifts. Adoption rates are stipulated; they are not observed customers or a test of the book.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy audience is 20 fans at 80% adoption and 80 other users at 20%. Combined expected adoption percentage? The weighted expected total is 20 × 0.8 + 80 × 0.2 = 32 of 100; the overall rate is 32%.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, selection, inputs [20, 80, 80, 20], output 32; independent Python recomputation.

claims.text: Does it hold up? The arithmetic follows our assumptions; real-world applicability and book attribution remain unverified.
claims.source: Scope limitation, not a research verdict: only original toy derivation supplied. Publication requires independently opened book chapter and separate real-world evidence review; no effectiveness inference is made.
